rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual cap
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the percent change in CPI over the most recent 12-month period; if CPI is negative, no increase is permitted. The City publishes the allowable increase annually by June 30, effective September 1.
rules.key_value: lower of 3% or 80% of CPI change over 12 months

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental units in buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before January 1, 1990.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Mobile home spaces first offered for rent after January 1, 1990 are exempt.

rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance (no section number given)
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.

rules.title: Santa Ana rent cap fair return petition
rules.requirement: Owners may petition for relief from the cap by showing that an increase above the annual allowance is necessary for a fair and reasonable return; the City Manager or designee decides within 60 days of a complete application.

coverage_conditions.summary: Owners of residential rental property or mobile home parks subject to the rent cap.

rules.interaction: Provides a relief mechanism from the annual rent cap.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance (no section number given)
rules.quoted_span: Any owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the cap, but will need to provide evidence that a rate increase in excess of the annual allowance is necessary to provide a fair and reasonable return for their property.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice. At-fault causes include nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance and criminal activity; no-fault causes include owner occupancy, withdrawal from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel. Owners must first give notice of a violation with time to cure before a for-cause termination.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies after 30 days, except housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories and other shared living quarters.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Excludes deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories and other shared living quarters.

rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (no section number given)
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: Santa Ana no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.key_value: 3 months of relocation assistance or 3 months' rent waived

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies terminated for no-fault just cause in properties covered by the Just Cause Ordinance.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Excludes deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories and other shared living quarters.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the Just Cause Ordinance: housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (no section number given)
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
